subject: Clarifying log residency, retention, and forensics scope after incident
messages:
From: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@acme-payments.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify log residency & retention after last week's incident

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the quick response last week. The security team has a few outstanding questions we need answered for our board and our insurance carrier regarding post-incident evidence handling:

- Where are the server and application logs for our Dedicated cluster physically stored (region/availability zone)?
- What is the default retention window for the different log classes (access logs, application logs, audit logs, runtime trace)?
- Can Redwood produce a cryptographically verifiable export of logs (hash manifest + S3/rsync snapshot) for forensic review? If so, what is the expected delivery SLA?
- If we request deletion of specific artifacts after the investigation, what is the deletion workflow and how do you provide proof-of-deletion (cert, log entry, KMS key rotation evidence)?
- Will Redwood place a legal/technical hold to prevent deletion until we confirm no further need for evidence? If so, what are the timelines and operational impacts?

I've attached a short incident summary. Tim and I need a concise Q&A by end of day Wednesday so we can finalize the carrier form.

Attachments: incident_summary_acme.pdf (PDF, 1.1 MB)

Regards,
Alice Byrne
Head of Security, Acme Payments

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme-payments.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify log residency & retention after last week's incident

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (infra) and Marissa (security/compliance) to provide the technical and policy details. We'll aim to get a short Q&A back to you by EOD Wednesday.

Initial notes:
- Acme is running in a Dedicated pool that we provisioned in eu-west-1 per your onboarding request (we'll confirm AZ-level placement in the export manifest).
- Default retention for Dedicated customers is configurable; the standard template is 180 days for access/audit logs and 90 days for application traces, but contract overrides can apply.
- We can perform a forensics export and produce a signed manifest (SHA-256 hashes), plus a time-stamped export stored in a customer-specific S3 bucket. Dev will outline the exact steps and expected SLA.
- Redwood's deletion workflow includes an admin request, internal approval, and an automated wipe of objects followed by a signed deletion certificate; Marissa will attach the template.
- We can activate a technical hold (suspend scheduled deletion/retention policies) immediately for the Acme tenancy until the hold is cleared — that will prevent automated purges but does not block customer-initiated copy operations.

Attached: residency_matrix.csv (high-level mapping of artifact types to storage/retention).

-Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@acme-payments.com>, Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify log residency & retention after last week's incident

Thanks, Rachel. Technical details below (keeping it short).

Storage/residency:
- Customer tenancy for Acme is provisioned into our Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1. Primary storage for logs is in eu-west-1 S3 buckets owned by Redwood but tagged and isolated per-tenant. Snapshots are retained in the same region; cross-region replication is not enabled for Acme unless requested.

Retention (current active config):
- Access/audit logs (control plane + API): 180 days (rolling window)
- Application logs (stdout/stderr from runtime): 90 days
- Runtime traces/kv-cache traces: 30 days by default (large volume; we usually keep shorter windows)

Forensics export process (what we can deliver):
1) Freeze: we pause automatic deletion/retention jobs for the Acme buckets and create a read-only snapshot.
2) Snapshot export: produce a time-stamped tarball of the relevant prefixes (access/, audit/, app/) and upload to a customer-controlled S3 endpoint we provide (or provide a pre-signed download for immediate pull).
3) Manifest: compute SHA-256 hashes for each file and sign the manifest with our internal signing key. We can also provide an HMAC verified against the customer's provided key material if you prefer.
4) Chain-of-custody: export includes an export log (who requested, who ran, checksums) and a short PDF containing the UTC timestamp and operation metadata.

SLA/ETA: 3 business days to produce an initial export after scope confirmation and access authorization. Larger exports (multi-GB/TB) may require up to 10 business days.

Deletion proof:
- We perform object deletion and then run a secure wipe for underlying objects where supported; we provide a signed deletion certificate with object keys and deletion timestamps. For S3, we include versioned deletion markers and a hash-of-hashes to show removal. If Acme requests key rotation (KMS), we can include KMS audit logs as additional proof.

Notes/constraints:
- For Dedicated customers with strict residency, all work happens in eu-west-1. If Acme needs artifacts to be exported outside EU for carrier review, we need written authorization (and we will note that in the export manifest).
- We do not keep user plaintext secrets in logs, but some runtime traces may contain truncated user-level data; we can run a redaction pass pre-export if requested (adds 1–2 business days).

Attaching a short ops-runbook for the export: forensic_export_instructions.md

- Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@acme-payments.com>, Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 17 May 2027 00:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify log residency & retention after last week's incident

Adding the compliance side.

Policy & legal hold:
- We will place a technical hold on scheduled deletions for the Acme tenancy immediately when requested by the Acme security contact (Alice). That hold remains in place until Acme issues written release (email is sufficient) or legal instructs otherwise.
- Holds are visible in the Console under "Retention Holds" and include start time, owner, and reason. While on hold, normal retention jobs skip the affected prefixes.

Deletion process & evidence:
- Deletion workflow: 1) Customer deletion request -> 2) Internal approvals (security + legal) -> 3) Scheduled wipe job -> 4) Signed deletion certificate generation. The certificate includes object keys, timestamps, operator ID, and a SHA-256 hash-of-hashes.
- Certificate template attached (deletion_cert_template.docx). We can also provide a notarized letter through our legal team on request (adds ~5 business days).

Recommended immediate next steps for Acme:
1) Confirm scope of the export (which prefixes/date ranges).
2) Confirm whether export may leave EU (carrier often needs copies in US); if not, we keep everything in eu-west-1.
3) Request technical hold in writing so Dev's team can freeze deletion windows.

If you want, we can produce a concise Q&A PDF for your carrier by Wednesday EOD with the points above summarized.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@acme-payments.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme-payments.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 May 2027 02:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify log residency & retention after last week's incident

Rachel / team — this is helpful, thank you. A few quick clarifications:

- We confirm scope: access/, audit/, and app/ prefixes for the period 2027-05-09 through 2027-05-15.
- Please keep export artifacts within eu-west-1 (carrier can accept EU-stored copies).
- We request a technical hold effective immediately. I'll send the holding request from security@acme-payments.com now.
- We would like the signed manifest + deletion certificate once any later deletion occurs. Also please put an initial export into a customer-controlled S3 bucket (we will provide the destination and credentials).

If you can deliver the initial export and manifest within 3 business days per Dev's SLA, and produce the Q&A PDF for our carrier by Wednesday EOD, that will close the majority of our open asks.

Alice Byrne
Head of Security, Acme Payments
